inputs.original_text: DSD athletes also face exclusion from future Olympics IOC says move will protect fairness and safety’ The International Olympic Committee has banned transgender women and DSD athletes from the female category of events at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and future Games in a landmark decision. Kirsty Coventry, president of the IOC, said: “It would not be fair for biological males to compete in the female category.” Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: The IOC is turning exclusion into official policy: transgender women and DSD athletes will be barred from the female category at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and future Games. Calling it “fairness and safety” doesn’t make the decision neutral; it shifts the burden onto already marginalized athletes while offering no supporting detail for that justification. Kirsty Coventry’s claim that “It would not be fair for biological males to compete in the female category” reduces a complex eligibility question to a sweeping label. This is institutional power deciding whose participation is acceptable—and the costs fall on trans and DSD athletes.
